source_text: In Hausa communities of northern Nigeria and southern Niger, traditional defenses of gishiri cutting portray it as a vital ethnomedical intervention to address "gishiri disease," a culturally recognized condition involving perceived vaginal narrowing that manifests as dyspareunia, infertility, amenorrhea, genital prolapse, or obstructed labor. [36] [28]
